# The required check set (#3971)
#
# WHAT THIS IS. The named list of check runs that decide whether a head SHA is
# reviewable. `required_check_state` (scripts/agents/lib/gh_project.sh) reads
# this file, matches the names EXACTLY against the check runs GitHub reports
# for a commit, and answers one of:
#
#   failed  - a required check on that head concluded failure. The head is the
#             developer's problem: `developer_submit_for_review.sh` refuses to
#             submit it, and `claude-code-review.yml` hands it back instead of
#             spending a review invocation relaying what the PR page already
#             shows.
#   pending - a required check is present and has not concluded. Nobody's
#             problem yet: the review trigger WAITS. A PR that is merely
#             mid-CI is never bounced back to the developer.
#   absent  - no required check is present on the head at all. Bounded grace
#             only (the checks have not been created yet); after it, treated
#             as clear.
#   clear   - every required check present on the head passed.
#
# WHY A NAMED LIST AND NOT "EVERY CHECK ON THE HEAD". Four of the checks on a
# PR head belong to the review itself (`head-gate`, `claude-review`,
# `head-not-reviewable`, `execute-review-decision`): gating on them deadlocks
# the gate against its own run -- `head-gate` cannot be complete at the moment
# `head-gate` decides. The rest of the not-required list is project bookkeeping — adding a card
# to the project board, stamping a lane, detecting a conflict. A flake in any
# of those must not be able to wedge the pipeline, and none of them says
# anything about whether the code is correct.
#
# ABSENT IS NOT PENDING. Most jobs below are path-filtered, so on any given PR
# most of them never run. A required check that is not attached to the head is
# not waited for and not counted against it — the path filter already decided
# it does not apply. This is what keeps the list safe to extend: naming a check
# here costs nothing on the PRs it does not run on.
#
# MAINTENANCE. Every job of every `pull_request`- or
# `pull_request_target`-triggered workflow must appear
# in exactly one of the two sections below — `tests/unit/test_required_checks.py`
# fails otherwise, in both directions (a name here that matches no job, and a
# job that this file never classified). A new smoke workflow therefore cannot
# be added without deciding whether it gates review.
#
# NAMES ARE CHECK-RUN NAMES, not job ids: a job with a `name:` reports under
# that name. `Install the working tree's formulas` is macos-brew-smoke.yml's
# `keg-install` job. The test above resolves both forms.

[required]
# Always runs on every PR (no path filter) — the presence signal the grace
# period keys on.
security-scan

# Quality gates for the paths they cover.
terraform-aws-validate
validate-web

# ci-tests.yml's three jobs (#4209). Required, and they are newly classifiable
# at all: until 2026-10-22 that workflow had no `pull_request` trigger and
# every job was `if: github.ref == RELEASE_BRANCH`, so `ruff`, `black`, `mypy`,
# `pytest`, `tsc`, `eslint` and `vitest --coverage` -- every step that file
# labels "(blocking)" -- were only ever evaluated AFTER the merge that broke
# them. A gate that cannot attach to a PR head cannot be a required check for
# one, which is why this list did not name them; now that it can, not naming
# them would mean the review does not wait for the suite it is reviewing.
#
# All three self-scope on the diff (`scripts/ci/diff_scope.py`) and report a
# definite conclusion either way, so on a PR they are never `absent` -- they
# are present and green with their steps skipped. A push to a feature branch
# ALSO leaves a `skipped` run of each on the same head (the `if:` above): that
# is "did not apply", which this file's header already covers, and the
# PR-event run is the one carrying the answer.
test
determinism
web
# web-gate-smoke.yml (#4209). All three required, and path-filtered to the
# gate's own surface so they are absent -- and free -- on essentially every
# PR. The first plants a failing web test and then an uncovered branch in the
# real suite and requires the real command to fail on each, then requires it
# to pass with the branch covered; the second reverts `ci-tests.yml` to its
# push-only shape and requires the tree-wide guard to fail. A red one means
# the 100% coverage gate is back to being declared and not evaluated, which is
# the state v3.0.1 was in for the whole of its life before this.
#
# The third is the other direction, from this issue's review round: a gate
# that now runs on a PR head is a gate that can be red for the WRONG reason.
# It deletes a real web file and a real test file and requires the raw tools
# to be red on those paths and the two blocking steps to be green on the same
# diff -- so a PR that removes an admin screen (#3803, #3804 and #3805 each
# did) is not handed a failure its change does not have.
the-web-gate-blocks-a-regression
the-gate-guards-are-not-vacuous
a-deleted-file-does-not-redden-the-gate

# Smoke jobs. These are this project's executed-verification evidence (D-006);
# a red one is a real defect on the head, which is precisely what the developer
# round must fix rather than the reviewer relay.

# owner, or the rule the owner set about labels, is broken on this head.

# escalation-headline-smoke.yml (#4176). Both required. The first is the

# pruned, and that the resulting headline names the red base instead of "error
# type could not be determined" -- each proven in both directions. The second
# is the pure decision table plus that suite. A red one means an escalation is
# back to telling the owner nothing, which is the state #4166 was filed from.
the-4166-run-reproduced
the-pure-decisions-and-the-shell-suite
# red-head-round-smoke.yml (#4179). Required. It is the executed evidence that
# a submission refused for a red head CONTINUES the developer round instead of
# escalating -- proven in both directions: the pre-#4179 Phase 2 `case` is run
# and must still exit FATAL for `ci_red`, the run-log API is asked mid-run for
# the premise, and the workflow's own auto-retry/escalation `if:` expressions
# are evaluated over a ci_red round's outputs. A red one means the pipeline is
# back to waking the owner for a class it calls retriable, which is the state
# #4138 was escalated from.
the-4138-round-reproduced
# release-prereq-smoke.yml (#4166). Both required. The first is the executed
# evidence that Phase 0 provisions BEFORE it decides the gate and stops before
# Phase 1 when it cannot -- the ordering is what keeps a signed-off release
# from dying after master, the tag and PyPI are already public. The second is
# the proof that adding a sprint iteration does not wipe the owner's board,
# which the owner made binding before any ceremony code was allowed to touch
# project 2; a red one means that permission no longer holds.
Phase 0 inventories, provisions, then gates — in that order
Adding a sprint iteration does not wipe board item values
The guard refuses the branch that holds the only copy
A merge that cannot be verified does not close its issue
A failed verification continues the work, it does not restart it

# image-build-fetch-policy-smoke.yml (#4205). Required. It is the executed
# evidence that a build which cannot reach the package registry fails loudly
# and is attributed to the registry -- and the only job here that builds with
# the network OFF. Every other image-building smoke builds with it on, which
# is why `npm ci` exiting 0 over an empty node_modules went unnoticed: those
# jobs are green by luck on this path. A red one means either the silent
# failure is back or the attribution broke, and both are the defect.
image-build-fetch-policy-smoke
# glitchtip-worker-smoke.yml (#4208). Required. It is the executed evidence
# that `glitchtip-worker` is Ready only while its consumer consumes, and it is
# fault-injected in both directions: the run FAILS unless the start-up wedge
# reproduces, unless the heartbeat probe this repo shipped until #4208 calls
# that wedged worker healthy, and unless the new probe calls it broken. A
# green that proves nothing is the failure mode it exists to prevent -- the
# race is between two containers coming up, so a fast runner hides it, which
# is how the defect reached acceptance twice. A red one means either the
# start-up gate or the probe is gone, and the half-dead state is invisible
# again.
#
# The same job also carries #4212's executed evidence: that the pinned image
# reads every variable the two substrates set on it, that it has no reader at
# all for the `CELERY_*` pair they used to carry, that `VTASKS_QUEUES` is
# inert from the environment while `VTASKS_CONCURRENCY` is not, and that the
# default concurrency fits the worker's memory limit -- the measurement behind
# leaving it at the default. A red one there means a comment on one of the
# manifests has become false.
glitchtip-worker is Ready only when consuming, and reads its config

# macos-brew-smoke.yml's `candidate-upgrade` job (#4133). Required, and
# deliberately on a different footing from `Install the working tree's
# formulas` below: that one is advisory because it was red somewhere new on
# every run, which is a gate measuring itself. This one answers a single
# question with two measured halves -- with the comparison reverted the
# surfaces report [OK] over a process running a deleted venv, and restored
# they name it and repair it -- so a red run is a statement about the head,
# not about the runner. It is the executed evidence (D-006) that a candidate
# upgrade on a running stack leaves the api on the new keg's interpreter,
# which is the whole of #4133; advisory, it would prove nothing on the PR
# that broke it.

# triggers (`ensure_project_hygiene.yml`, `pr_project_status_on_close.yml`) is
# not vacuous: it goes red on a PR-head checkout, a `gh pr checkout`, a
# dependency install, a revert to `pull_request` in either file, and a newly
# planted `pull_request` workflow reading a secret. Required and path-filtered,
# so it is absent (and free) on essentially every PR; when it does run, a red
# one means the only thing standing between an arbitrary author's branch and a
# `workflow`-scoped PAT has stopped working.

# acceptance-sweep-dispatch-smoke.yml's first job (#4201). Required, and
# path-filtered to the two sweep workflows plus the helper and its callers, so
# it is absent -- and free -- on essentially every PR. When it does run it is
# the executed evidence that removing the `*/30` crons did not strand the
# sweeps: the argv shape, the `--ref` that stops a dispatch silently running
# the default branch's copy, the best-effort contract, and the promotion
# cascade converging in one run -- each re-planted in its pre-fix form to
# prove the assertion can fail. A red one means a merge, ceremony or gate
# release no longer starts the sweep that promotes the owner's work.
helper-behaves

# on the PRs it does not run for -- absent is not pending.

# macos-brew-smoke.yml's `mac-model-backend` job (#4150): `brew install
# ollama`, `brew services start ollama` and `nyxgpt ops required-models`
# executed on a real macos-15 runner, with the install-without-pull near-miss
# measured in between.
#
# REQUIRED, unlike its `keg-install` sibling below, and the difference is
# deliberate. That job was demoted for failing somewhere new on every run --
# it was measuring itself. This one is path-filtered to four cold files (the
# two user-data templates, `model_bootstrap.py`, this workflow), so it is
# absent -- and therefore free -- on essentially every PR, and when it does
# run it is measuring the one thing the change touched.
#
# And it is required because the whole of #4150 is that nothing executed this
# path: an EC2 Mac deploy exited 0 onto a machine that could not answer a chat
# message, through green CI, because no job installed the model backend. A
# guard against that filed as advisory is the same gap with a job attached to
# it.
The model backend, installed and pulled on real macOS
# pipefail-pipeline-smoke.yml's `pipeline-readers-drain` job (#4192, review
# round 2). Required, and deliberately wide-filtered: it is the only thing
# standing between the gate surface and a check whose colour is not evidence
# about the head. `brew services list | grep -q "$KEG"` turned its own SUCCESS
# into a red required check (run 38071858945) because `grep -q` left on the
# first match and brew's next write took EPIPE, which `pipefail` reported as
# the pipeline's status; the same head was green an hour before. The predicate
# form is worse and silent -- `launchctl list | grep -q` reads a lost race as
# "not loaded", so the step skips the half it exists to prove and then passes
# on a service that survived. This job runs the mechanism, both repaired steps
# against a stub producer that loses the race on purpose, and the tree-wide
# scan. A red one means a gate somewhere can now go red (or quietly pass) for
# a reason that has nothing to do with the commit.
pipeline-readers-drain
# pipefail-pipeline-smoke.yml's `pytest-jobs-can-collect` job (#4192, review
# round 3), and the job above is the defect that filed it. Added as a required
# check by round 2, `pipeline-readers-drain` installed `pyyaml pytest` and ran
# `pytest tests/unit/...`, which loads the ROOT `tests/conftest.py` ->
# `tests/log_guard.py` -> `psutil`. It exited 4 at COLLECTION -- a usage
# error, not a test failure -- so the check was red with every assertion it
# exists for untested, on a head that was fine. That took the PR to a
# hand-back and then to an owner escalation.
#
# Fifteen jobs across eleven workflows make this same decision, three
# different ways, and nothing on the tree checked any of them. This job holds
# all of them to one rule -- a pytest call that loads the root conftest needs
# `pip install -e .`, or it says `--noconftest` -- derived from the conftest's
# own imports, so there is no restated dependency list to drift. Required
# because the failure it prevents is precisely a red required check that says
# nothing about the commit, which is the state this whole issue was filed
# from; and cheap, because it is the same wide path filter as its sibling and
# runs in about a minute on ubuntu-latest.
pytest-jobs-can-collect
# macos-brew-smoke.yml's `restart-wait` job (#4192). Required, and the only
# job in that workflow that does not run on a Mac -- which is the point. The
# `keg-install` step driving #4043's self-restart failed on 9 of its last 10
# PR runs because it sampled the api's pid one second after an endpoint that
# answers `{"status":"scheduled"}` by design, and nothing on the tree could
# see that: the logic is workflow YAML, executed only by an ADVISORY macOS
# job. This job extracts that shell out of the workflow and runs it against a
# stub launchctl in both directions in ~40s on Linux, path-filtered like the
# rest of the workflow. A red one means a restart step here is measuring the
# machine before the restart lands -- i.e. a gate about to report a product
# defect that is not there.
The restart steps wait for the restart instead of sampling it

[not-required]
# macos-brew-smoke.yml's `keg-install` job. Owner decision, 2026-08-24: this
# was [required] and had been red on EVERY run for 24+ hours, across several
# branches, failing at a DIFFERENT step each time -- #3854's caveats
# assertion, then #3861's keg-venv copy, then #3854 again. A gate that fails
# somewhere new each run is not measuring the change under review; it is
# measuring itself, and it blocked every PR behind it including #4036, whose
# own ollama-logs proof step sits later in this same job and had therefore
# never executed once.
#
# The job still RUNS and still reports on every PR -- this only stops it
# gating merges. macOS keg installs remain covered, just not as a veto.
#
# REVISIT: put this back under [required] as soon as the job is green twice in
# a row on unrelated PRs. It is the executed evidence for the macOS install
# path (D-006), so leaving it advisory indefinitely would quietly retire a
# gate the release depends on.
#
# STATE, recorded 2026-10-04 (#4121), because the REVISIT above has never been
# met and the consequence had to be written down rather than inferred:
#
#   **The macOS install path has no executed gate at all today.** This job is
#   the only one that installs the formulas on a real Mac, and it is advisory.
#   `published-tap` below is [required] but cannot gate a PR either -- it is
#   `if: inputs.formula_version != ''`, so it never attaches to a PR head, and
#   at an rc cut it runs *after* the tap push, which
#   `release-publish-pypi.yml` deliberately does not gate on. So between
#   2026-08-24 and now, a change could break `brew install` on macOS and merge
#   green. #4122 and #4121 both did.
#
#   Not repaired here on purpose. The job's failures since 2026-08-24 have been
#   at a different step each time and none of them is this issue's defect;
#   "repair keg-install" is a separate diagnosis from "stop the macOS install
#   failing", and bundling them would mean changing a gate on the strength of a
#   guess (first principle 4). What the job does now carry is #4122's
#   truststore fault injection, landed on the round that diagnosed the
#   sandbox, so the evidence for the install path exists and is cited even
#   while the job is advisory.
#
#   The bar to flip it stands as written above: green twice in a row on
#   unrelated PRs.
#
# WHY IT WAS RED THROUGH 2026-10-10, diagnosed on #4192 and recorded because
# "failing at a different step each time" above was the reason it is advisory
# and that reason had never been examined: the last ten PR runs all failed at
# the SAME step, `The api restarts itself when the UI asks it to (#4043)`, and
# the defect was in the step rather than in the keg. It read the api's pid one
# second after `POST /infra/restart-required`, which answers
# `{"status":"scheduled"}` by design, so `up` returned against the process
# that had not been replaced yet. The pid change is the wait condition now.
# That is one cause removed, not the whole history; the bar above is unchanged
# and this job stays advisory until it is met on unrelated PRs, because
# flipping a gate on two passes of the PR that touched it is the trade this
# section already refused once.
Install the working tree's formulas

# The review's own runs, including the gate itself. Requiring any of them
# deadlocks the gate against itself: `claude-review` cannot be complete at the
# moment the gate decides whether to start `claude-review`, and `head-gate` is
# still running while it asks. (This is the deadlock Q-005 raises for the merge
# path; the merge path is untouched here.)
claude-review
head-gate
head-not-reviewable
execute-review-decision


# Project bookkeeping. None of these judges the code, and a flake in one must
# not hold a green PR out of review.
add-to-project
closure-hygiene
# `pr-hygiene` and `stamp-closed-lane` are also the two `pull_request_target`
# jobs (#4167), and such a run is associated with the BASE commit rather than
# the PR head. `required_check_state` matches names against the head's check
# runs, so requiring either would hold every head at `absent`/`pending`. They
# were already bookkeeping; this is a second, independent reason not to flip
# them.
pr-hygiene
delete-abandoned-branch
link-revert-to-issue
stamp-closed-lane
detect
resolve

# acceptance-sweep-dispatch-smoke.yml's live half (#4201). Advisory, and the
# split from its `helper-behaves` sibling is deliberate. The PROPERTY -- that
# every actor dispatches, through one helper, naming the release branch -- is
# required above and is a statement about the head. This job additionally
# performs a real `dry_run=true` dispatch and polls for the resulting run, so
# it can go red for two reasons that are not about the change under review:
# GitHub's dispatch-to-run latency exceeding the poll, and a context with no
# `SCRUMMASTER_AGENT_TOKEN` (it warns and passes in that case rather than
# claiming a disproof it did not make). It still RUNS and still prints the run
# URLs to the step summary, which is what makes it the citable executed
# evidence for the trigger -- this only stops an Actions hiccup wedging the
# pipeline behind it.
dispatch-reaches-the-sweeps
